newsitem.title: FRANCE: CYCLING-FACTFILE ON TOUR DE FRANCE WINNER ULLRICH.
newsitem.headline: CYCLING-FACTFILE ON TOUR DE FRANCE WINNER ULLRICH.

text.p: Factfile on Germany's Jan Ullrich,
who won the Tour de France on Sunday:
-- born December 2, 1973 in Rostock, then East Germany.
Brought up by mother Marianne after father left home when he was
three
-- 1986 joined the East German National Sports School
-- 1987 joined Peter Becker's Dynamo Berlin cycling team.
Becker took the youngster under his wing.
-- 1993 won world amateur road race championship in Oslo.
-- 1994 with Becker acting as agent, signed for the Deutsche
Telekom team under Belgian manager Walter Godefroot. Came third
behind winner Chris Boardman of Britain in the world time trial
championship in Sicily.
-- 1996 took part in first Tour de France, emerging into the
limelight with victory in penultimate stage time trial in St
Emilion outside Bordeaux. He beat Spaniard Miguel Indurain by 56
seconds and eventual Tour winner and team mate Bjarne Riis of
Denmark by more than two minutes. Finished second overall.
-- 1997 raced in second Tour, taking yellow jersey with
victory in the 10th stage in a remarkable climb of the Arcalis
peak in Andorra. Another stage win in the St Etienne time trial
three days later helped him significantly to his eventual
victory.
